E2dat1.title: Sorting and showing data in tables and graphs
E2dat1.concept: Sort things by a rule and count them; a **table** or a **graph** lets you compare at a glance.

E4dat1.title: Reading line graphs
E4dat1.concept: A **line graph** shows how a value changes over time with points and lines. Going up means an increase, going down a decrease.
E4dat1.example: 12 on day 1 → 20 on day 3: up by 8

E5dat1.title: Finding the mean
E5dat1.concept: The **mean** is the sum of the data divided by how many there are.

E5dat2.title: Chance
E5dat2.concept: The **chance** of an event is a number from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain): chance = (favourable cases) ÷ (all cases).
E5dat2.example: 3 A-balls, 2 B-balls → chance of A is $\frac{3}{5}=0.6$

E6dat1.title: Band graphs and pie charts
E6dat1.concept: **Band graphs** and **pie charts** treat the whole as 100% and show each part's share. Part = whole × share.

M1neg1.title: Integers and rational numbers
M1neg1.concept: Same signs: add the absolute values. Different signs: subtract them and keep the sign of the larger. For × and ÷ the result is + if the signs match and − if not.

M1fac1.title: Prime factorisation, GCD and LCM
M1fac1.concept: Writing a number as a product of primes is **prime factorisation**. The largest shared divisor is the **greatest common divisor**, the smallest shared multiple the **least common multiple**.

M1crd1.title: The coordinate plane
M1crd1.concept: A point is written (x, y). The signs decide Quadrants 1–4, and reflecting in the x-axis flips the sign of y.

M1prp1.title: Direct and inverse proportion
M1prp1.concept: **Direct proportion** is y=ax and **inverse proportion** is $y=\frac{a}{x}$. In direct proportion y÷x is constant; in inverse proportion x×y is constant.

M1sta1.title: Averages and relative frequency
M1sta1.concept: The **median** is the middle value in order, the **mode** the most frequent value. **Relative frequency** = frequency ÷ total.

M2rec1.title: Repeating decimals
M2rec1.concept: A decimal whose digits repeat for ever is a **repeating decimal**; the repeating part is its **block**. A reduced fraction terminates only if its denominator has just the factors 2 and 5.

M2lfn1.title: Linear functions and linear equations
M2lfn1.concept: In y=ax+b, a is the slope and b the y-intercept. The intersection of two graphs is the solution of the two equations together.

el.econ1.title: Interest, exchange rates and tax
el.econ1.concept: Simple interest = principal × rate × years; compound amount = principal × (1 + rate)^years. An exchange rate is the value of 1 unit of a currency; tax is price × a percentage.

el.econ2.title: Demand, supply and optimisation
el.econ2.concept: Equilibrium is where the demand and supply curves meet. Maximum revenue R=pq and elasticity come from functions and derivatives.

el.ai1.title: Text and image data
el.ai1.concept: A document becomes a vector of word counts and an image a matrix of pixel values. The larger the dot product, the more alike two documents are.

el.ai2.title: Prediction and optimisation
el.ai2.concept: Predictions improve with a trend line's slope, the mean of squared errors (the loss) and gradient descent $x_{new}=x-\eta f'(x)$.

el.job1.title: Unit conversion and ratios
el.job1.concept: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 hour = 60 minutes. Sale price = price × (1 − discount); mixing in the ratio a:b gives A a share of $\frac{a}{a+b}$.

el.job2.title: Area, counting and growth
el.job2.concept: Area gives the material needed, the product rule the number of pairs, and (increase) ÷ (first value) × 100 the growth rate.

el.cul1.title: Mathematics in art and daily life
el.cul1.concept: The golden ratio is about 1.618; a note one octave up has twice the frequency; 6 braille dots give $2^6-1=63$ patterns; a majority is more than half.

el.cul2.title: Mathematics in society and the environment
el.cul2.concept: Means and growth rates let you analyse social and environmental problems mathematically. Growth rate = (increase) ÷ (first value) × 100.

el.sta1.title: Statistical questions and samples
el.sta1.concept: The standard deviation is the square root of the mean of squared deviations (the variance). Samples are drawn by random, stratified, cluster or systematic sampling.

el.sta2.title: Estimation and hypothesis tests
el.sta2.concept: The 95% margin of error is $1.96\times\frac{σ}{\sqrt{n}}$. If $|z|$ of $z=\frac{\bar{x}-\mu}{σ/\sqrt{n}}$ is above 1.96, reject the null hypothesis at the 5% level.

el.res1.title: Research methods
el.res1.concept: A mathematics research project can use literature research, case studies, mathematical experiments or development research.
el.res1.example: Rolling dice to find a pattern → experiment

el.res2.title: Research steps and ethics
el.res2.concept: Research goes topic → plan → carry out → present → reflect. Citing sources and never altering results is research ethics.
el.res2.example: After the topic comes the research plan

E3ari1.title: Adding and subtracting three-digit numbers
E3ari1.concept: Work from the ones place. If a column adds up to 10 or more, **carry** to the next place; if you cannot subtract, **borrow** from the next place.

E6ari1.title: Mixed calculations
E6ari1.concept: When the four operations are mixed, work out **the brackets** first, then **multiplication and division**, and finally **addition and subtraction**, from left to right.

E6ari2.title: Rounding up, down and to the nearest
E6ari2.concept: **Rounding up** raises the number to the next multiple, **rounding down** drops the lower digits, and **rounding to the nearest** raises it only if the next digit is 5 or more.
E6ari2.example: 3472 to a multiple of 100: up 3500, down 3400, nearest 3500

M3sta1.title: Variance and standard deviation
M3sta1.concept: The **deviation** is (value) − (mean). The **variance** is the mean of the squared deviations and the **standard deviation** is its positive square root. The larger it is, the more spread out the data are.

H2seq1.title: Sums of sequences and ∑
H2seq1.concept: $\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k$ means $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n$. Useful rules: $\sum k=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$, $\sum c=cn$ and $\sum(a_k+b_k)=\sum a_k+\sum b_k$.

H3pro1.title: The addition rule and complements
H3pro1.concept: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$. The probability of the complement is $P(A^c)=1-P(A)$.
